page.layout: One page of text in a single column, with no headings. Right margin shows only show-through from the other side of the leaf, which is not transcribed. Running head at top. Signature and catchword at the foot.

main_text.p: bant, & in occasiones erant intenti: quas ex voto nacti bellum ei simul denunciarunt & intulerunt. Occasionum praecipuae erant hae. Laborabant ea aetate factionibus civilibus Carthaginienses, & cladem ingentem recens acceperant a Masinisa[?] rege vicino, & Utica post[?] Carthaginem in ista Africae ora urbs maxima, non longe a Carthagine disjuncta, & iisdem cum ea conditoribus Tyriis orta, eo ipso tempore quo haec versabant Romani, sua omnia sponte Romanis dediderant. Ob quae perculsi Carthaginienses missis semel iterumque Romam legatis ad satisfaciendum, si quid ab se desideraretur, senatui se obtulerunt. Responsum iis publicum lubrice[?], deinde ut consulibus, qui jam Siciliam cum exercitu trajecerant, intra dies xxx pueros totius civitatis nobilissimos ccc fidei obsides darent, aliaque quae imperaturi consules essent, facerent, si declinare bellum, & retinere libertatem vellent. Haec Carthaginem perlata in summam maestitiam conjecere civitatem: sed quoniam urgebat necessitas, & parendi mora noxia esse posse putabatur, postulato duro mos est gestus, pueri etiam ante praestitutum diem per legatos eodem ad consules adducti, non sine ingenti dolore & planctu[?]

page.notes: Show-through from the reverse side is visible in the right margin and along the lower right (fragments of figures and words such as "uo" and "ɔu-"). It is not transcribed. Doubtful readings: "post" in "Utica post Carthaginem" is partly obscured by show-through; "lubrice" is hard to read; "Masinisa" has a mark over the a that may be an abbreviation; "planctu" at the foot is partly cut off by show-through. The ligature in "adducti" is read as ct.
